$comment: The rewrite of an HTML string to a call of interpolate, judged by both editors alike: a trim call after the literal stays inside the call, on the format; a multi-dollar literal keeps its prefix, so a $name that was text stays text; and a value in the body of a style, which interpolate refuses as a String, is passed as Trusted(...), where interpolate and Trusted are core's names in the file. The format is the corpus's: fixes holds the whole source after each quick fix, in the order offered.

cases.name: a literal with trimIndent keeps the trim inside the call

x

""".trimIndent()

x

""".trimIndent(), a, b).text

x

""".trimIndent(), a, b).text

cases.name: a value in a multi-dollar literal joined to a plain one is shown and marked with that literal's dollars

issues.message: Kotlin writes $${b} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(b: String) = interpolate("
" + $$"

%s

", b).text

import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted fun f(b: String) = "
" + $$"

$${Trusted(b)}

"
